name: Blue slate
lede: Blue slate is a cool grey named for the roofing stone, documented in Ridgway's 1912 standards and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system.

sections.title: The stone, greyed down
sections.body:
Our library carries Blue slate from Ridgway's 1912 color standards and the 1955 ISCC-NBS system, which classes it as a grayish blue [1]. It is a modifier on [[slate]], the rock split into roofing tiles, rather than a separate material [1]. Two near-duplicates from the same Ridgway plates sit close by in hue: [[deep-slate-blue]] and [[dusky-slate-blue]], both darker [1].

At LCH lightness 44 and chroma 5, it reads as almost neutral; our library's closest match by distance is [[black-coral]] [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Blue slate in 474 of 23,781 paintings (1.99 percent), as photographed [2]. It peaks in the 1900s, in 30 of 1,674 paintings, at twice the archive's overall rate for that century, and Claude Monet used it most, 5.4 times what his home museums' baseline predicts [2]. It most often plays a mid-tone inside a painting, and keeps company with Squirrel Grey far more than chance would suggest [2]. The earliest dated match, from 1100, is eight centuries older than the 1912 record, a floor set by a thin early archive, not a claim about the pigment's age [2].
